newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: FOCUS - Slovenian private bank seeks listing abroad.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Slovenian private bank seeks listing abroad.

text.p: Slovenia's second biggest bank SKB Banka d.d. is seeking to become the first company in the country to be listed abroad, Slovenian news agency STA reported on Thursday.
STA, quoting an SKB statement only released to local media, said the bank had already approached Nomura International and the Bank of New York to act as advisors in its bid for a listing.

Banking sources in London told Reuters SKB was planning to issue global depository receipts (GDRs), which may eventually represent up to 29 percent of its capital as part of the bank's longer term strategy of diversifying its shareholder base.
The sources said Nomura would lead the issue while Bank of New York would act as the depository bank.
SKB, Slovenia's largest private bank, declined to make any immediate comment to Reuters.

The bank's plan will have to be approved by shareholders at a meeting scheduled for November 14. The bank also has to win permission from the Bank of Slovenia to increase its current maximum holding by foreign shareholders from 30 percent to 49 percent.

Cvetka Selsek, SKB's executive director of international banking, said in an interview with Reuters in June that the bank was considering an international listing in order to raise the price of its shares.
The bank believed its share price was low due to the poor liquidity of the Slovenian market, she said.
SKB shares have risen sharply in recent weeks on rumours of a possible foreign listing. The stock has soared 45 percent since the end of September, closing at 43,630 tolars on Thursday.
Sources close to the bank told Reuters it was unlikely the listing would take place before the beginning of 1997.
The European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) currently has 15 percent of SKB shares, with German investment company DEG holding five percent.
U.S. investment house Merrill Lynch holds four percent and the remaining shares are in the hands of Slovenian institutions and individual shareholders.
A foreign listing by SKB, possibly in London and New York, would follow the London stock exchange listing of Croatia's Zagrebacka Banka in June, the first bank from the former Yugoslavia to do so.
SKB, which has a market stake of 11.3 percent, is active in both corporate and retail banking in Slovenia and abroad and has its own brokerage and real estate agency.
Its pre-tax profit for the first half of 1996 jumped to 1.5 billion tolars ($10.9 million), compared to 382 million in the same period last year. Total assets are at around 134 billion.
"We expect our profit at the end of the year to be twice as high as last year," SKB management board member Andrej Cetinski said in July. SKB reported pre-tax profit of 943.4 million tolars in 1995.
